title: Datadog Bits AI vs Sentry Seer: On-Call Incident Response

body_markdown:
*Written by: Nimesh Chakravarthi, Co-founder & CTO, Struct*


## Key Takeaways


-


Datadog Bits AI and Sentry Seer cover different layers. Bits AI supports broad incident management inside Datadog. Seer focuses on code-level debugging inside Sentry.


-


Neither tool runs the full loop from alert to confirmed resolution. On-call engineers still spend 30–45 minutes manually stitching together context across tools.


-


Struct fills this gap by investigating every alert across Datadog, Sentry, and the rest of your stack, then posting root cause and suggested fixes directly in Slack.


-


Struct adds incident resolution verification through an automated ~1-minute loop that confirms fixes against observability data, a capability Bits AI and Seer do not provide.


-

## Datadog Bits AI vs Sentry Seer: Stack Layers They Cover


[Datadog Bits AI is an AI assistant embedded in the Datadog platform that investigates alerts across metrics, logs, traces, and infrastructure telemetry](https://datadoghq.com/blog/datadog-incident-response-ai-features) .[Sentry Seer is an AI debugging agent within Sentry that performs root cause analysis on code-level errors and exceptions using stack traces, spans, and connected telemetry](https://blog.sentry.io/introducing-seer-agent) .


[Bits AI operates at the platform level](https://datadoghq.com/blog/bits-ai-sre-deeper-reasoning) . It can investigate a Kubernetes pod failure, correlate a deploy with a latency spike, and page engineers through Datadog Incident Response. Seer operates at the application level. It traces an exception back to the exact source line and can open a fix PR via GitHub or GitLab. Bits AI focuses on incident management, on-call workflows, and infrastructure. Seer focuses on code debugging within Sentry’s telemetry.


Datadog has also[announced preview support for Sentry as a third-party integration](https://datadoghq.com/blog/bits-ai-sre-deeper-reasoning) . Bits AI can ingest Sentry data, so teams can run both tools together in some environments.


## The On-Call Gap: Why Investigation Still Takes 45 Minutes


On-call engineers still jump between tools because Bits AI only works inside Datadog and Seer only sees Sentry. The investigation workflow from alert to verified resolution remains manual.


[Datadog Bits AI SRE investigates using telemetry already sent to Datadog](https://codeables.dev/article/how-do-we-buy-and-roll-out-datadog-bits-ai-sre-investigations-and) , following existing RBAC and data boundaries. If errors originate in Sentry, infrastructure metrics live in CloudWatch, and code sits in GitHub, Bits AI cannot access full context without extra configuration.[Sentry Seer investigates using Sentry’s own telemetry](https://struct.ai/blog/struct-vs-sentry-seer) such as errors, spans, and profiles, with application logs and custom metrics still in alpha as of mid-2026.


During a critical 2 AM alert, the on-call engineer often spends 30–45 minutes switching between Datadog dashboards, Sentry issues, and GitHub before forming a root cause hypothesis. Those 45 minutes consume SLA time before remediation even begins.

Struct automatically investigates every alert the moment it fires. It correlates logs, metrics, traces, and code across Datadog, Sentry, and your broader stack. It then delivers root cause, impact, and suggested fixes in Slack before you open your laptop.


Struct acts as an agentic production on-call system that sits on top of your existing observability tools. It keeps Datadog and Sentry in place and automates the investigation layer between them. Key capabilities include:


-


**Automated first-pass investigation:** When an alert fires, Struct immediately starts an investigation and[correlates data across Datadog metrics, Sentry issues, cloud logs, and GitHub deploy history](https://struct.ai/blog/struct-vs-datadog) . This creates a single narrative instead of scattered clues.


-


**Dynamically generated dashboards:** Struct builds issue-specific timelines with supporting evidence and charts pulled from your observability tools. These dashboards give engineers a focused view of what changed and when.


-


**Slack-native conversational AI:** Engineers ask follow-up questions, test hypotheses, or request additional logs directly in Slack. The investigation stays in one place instead of spreading across multiple consoles.


-


**Custom runbooks:** Teams encode their investigation procedures so Struct follows the same steps senior engineers would. This standardizes first-pass investigation quality across the team.


-


**Incident resolution verification:** Struct’s Incident Tracker confirms that an incident is resolved by checking observability data against a ~1-minute automated verification loop. This creates a closed feedback loop that competitors do not offer.


The impact is tangible.[Arcana cut investigation time from 30 minutes to 2 minutes and reclaimed 56 engineer-hours per month](https://struct.ai/blog/struct-vs-datadog) .

## The 2 AM Incident Scenario Across Tools


During a 2 AM critical alert, Bits AI investigates inside Datadog and Seer highlights code issues inside Sentry. Struct completes the cross-stack investigation and posts root cause to Slack before the engineer fully engages.


**Scenario:** A fintech app’s checkout API error rate spikes. The alert pages the on-call engineer.


**With Datadog Bits AI:** The engineer opens Datadog, finds the Bits Investigation running, and reviews the hypothesis.[Bits correlates the error spike with a recent deploy and identifies a database connection pool exhaustion](https://datadoghq.com/blog/bits-ai-sre-deeper-reasoning) . The engineer still checks Sentry for the specific exception, verifies blast radius in CloudWatch, and manually confirms the fix after remediation. Total time to understanding: 15–20 minutes.


**With Sentry Seer:** The engineer opens Sentry and sees the error grouped with a[Seer root cause analysis pointing to a null pointer in the payment service](https://blog.sentry.io/introducing-seer-agent) . Seer suggests a fix and can open a PR. The engineer still lacks clear infrastructure context and switches to Datadog to inspect metrics and logs. Total time to understanding: 20–30 minutes.


**With Struct:** The engineer’s phone buzzes. By the time they open Slack, Struct has already correlated the Sentry exception with Datadog metrics showing a latency spike, identified the deploy that introduced the regression, and posted a root cause summary with a suggested fix in the incident thread. The engineer reviews the analysis, applies the fix, and Struct verifies resolution against observability data. Total time to understanding: about 5 minutes.

## Using Datadog Bits AI and Sentry Seer Together


Teams can run Seer for code-level debugging and Bits AI for broader incident context because Datadog can ingest Sentry data. This combination still leaves engineers responsible for manual correlation and does not automate the full investigation loop.


A complementary stack strategy often looks like this: Sentry for error tracking, Datadog for metrics and logs, and Bits AI for AI-assisted investigation within Datadog.[Datadog’s Bits Investigation supports Sentry as a third-party integration in preview](https://datadoghq.com/blog/bits-ai-sre-deeper-reasoning) . Engineers still connect findings across tools themselves and still lack resolution verification.[Struct ingests Sentry issues the moment they fire and correlates them with Datadog metrics, cloud infrastructure, GitHub deploy history, logs, traces, and other tools](https://struct.ai/blog/struct-vs-sentry-seer) . It automates both investigation and resolution verification.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the difference between Datadog Bits AI and Sentry Seer?


Datadog Bits AI is a broad AI assistant for incident response across the Datadog platform, handling metrics, logs, traces, and infrastructure. It can page engineers, create Jira tickets, and run investigations across the full Datadog telemetry surface. Sentry Seer is a focused AI debugging agent for code-level root cause analysis within Sentry’s error tracking. It traces exceptions back to specific source lines, scores issues for fixability, and can open a pull request with a proposed fix. The tools address different layers of the stack and increasingly work in a complementary way.


### Does Sentry Seer work with Datadog?


Seer operates directly on Sentry’s own telemetry, including errors, spans, profiles, and (in alpha) application logs. It does not natively query Datadog metrics or infrastructure data. Datadog Bits AI has announced preview support for Sentry as a third-party integration, which allows Sentry data to inform Bits investigations from the Datadog side. For true cross-stack correlation between Sentry and Datadog, Struct provides a dedicated solution that ingests Sentry issues and correlates them with Datadog metrics, cloud logs, and GitHub deploy history automatically.


### Which tool is better for on-call incident response?


Struct offers the strongest fit for automated, end-to-end investigation and incident resolution verification. Datadog Bits AI handles broad incident management within Datadog and completes investigations in roughly 3–4 minutes, yet it does not verify resolution after remediation. Sentry Seer focuses on code debugging and gates automation on a proprietary actionability score, so some issues still require manual initiation. Struct automates the full on-call loop from alert to verified resolution and works on top of both Datadog and Sentry at the same time.


### How much does Datadog Bits AI cost?


Datadog Bits AI is billed per investigation run as an add-on to a Datadog subscription. A third-party source reports pricing of approximately $500 per 20 conclusive investigations per month on an annual plan and $600 per 20 on a month-to-month basis. Inconclusive investigations are not billed. Total cost depends on your existing Datadog spend. Teams often start with a small pilot set of critical monitors before expanding coverage to manage costs.


### How much does Sentry Seer cost?


Sentry Seer costs $40 per active contributor per month, where an active contributor is anyone committing two or more pull requests in a connected repository during the billing period. This charge sits on top of a Sentry Business plan ($80/month) or Enterprise plan. The base Sentry Team plan lists at $26/month when billed annually with default prepaid data, but it does not include Seer. For a team of 20 active contributors, Seer adds $800/month to the Sentry bill before any event overage charges.


### Can Struct integrate with Datadog and Sentry?


Struct connects to Datadog metrics, logs, and traces as primary inputs and adds cross-stack investigation into Sentry, GitHub, AWS CloudWatch, GCP Logs, Azure, Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, and other tools. It ingests Sentry issues as they fire and correlates them with the rest of your stack automatically. Setup takes under 10 minutes. Teams connect their issue source (Slack or PagerDuty), code repository (GitHub), and observability context (Datadog and cloud logs), then Struct begins investigating.


### What is incident resolution verification?


Incident resolution verification is a closed-loop process that automatically confirms an incident is resolved by checking observability data. It replaces assumptions based on a successful deployment or a manually closed ticket. Struct’s Incident Tracker performs this verification on an approximately 1-minute automated loop, checking live telemetry against the pre-incident baseline before declaring an incident resolved. Datadog Bits AI and Sentry Seer do not perform this verification step.
